sets.name: Short messages
sets.about: Short, clear messages with times, numbers and places.

items.title: A voicemail
items.say: Hi Anna, it's Tom. I'm calling about tomorrow's lesson. Sorry, but I can't come at ten o'clock. I have a meeting at the bank. Could we move the lesson to two o'clock in the afternoon? Please text me back. I'll be at home all day. Also, I'll bring the book you lent me last week. Thanks a lot. Bye!

qs.q: What time can't Tom come?
Where is his meeting?

items.title: A station announcement
items.say: Attention please. The train to Manchester, platform four, is delayed by twenty minutes. It will now leave at five fifty. Passengers for Leeds, please go to platform nine. That train leaves at six o'clock. Please remember to take all your bags with you. The cafe on platform two is open until eight. Thank you for waiting.

qs.q: How late is the Manchester train?
Which platform is the Leeds train?

items.title: In the supermarket
items.say: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Green's Supermarket. Today we have a special offer on apples and oranges: two kilos for three pounds. The bakery is on your left, and it closes at four o'clock today. Please don't forget that the shop will be closed on Sunday because of the holiday. Thank you, and have a nice day.

qs.q: How much are two kilos of fruit?
Why will the shop be closed on Sunday?

items.title: My busy day
items.say: Today was a busy day. I got up at half past six and took the bus to school. My first lesson was at eight fifteen, with a group of teenagers. At one o'clock I had lunch with my friend Kate. In the afternoon I had two private students. Now I'm tired, so I'm going to cook pasta and watch a film.

qs.q: What time was the first lesson?
How many private students did she have?

sets.name: Everyday situations
sets.about: Longer messages from parents, schools and landlords, with more numbers.

items.title: A parent's voicemail
items.say: Hello, this is Mrs Brown, Lucy's mum. I'm afraid Lucy won't be able to come on Thursday because she's got a dentist appointment at four thirty. Would it be possible to have the lesson on Friday instead, maybe around five? If not, we can skip this week. Oh, and could you remind me how much I owe you for last month? I think it was a hundred and twenty pounds. Thanks very much.

qs.q: Why can't Lucy come on Thursday?
How much does Mrs Brown think she owes?

items.title: A school announcement
items.say: Good afternoon, parents. A reminder that the school trip to the science museum is next Wednesday, the 14th. The coach leaves at eight forty-five sharp, so please bring your child to the main gate by half past eight. Children should wear comfortable shoes and bring a packed lunch, but no sweets, please. The trip costs eleven pounds, and you can pay at the school office until Monday.

qs.q: When should children be at the main gate?
How much does the trip cost?

items.title: About a flat
items.say: Hi, I'm calling about the flat on Park Road. Yes, it's still available. It's got two bedrooms and a small balcony, and it's about ten minutes' walk from the station. The rent is nine hundred pounds a month, and the bills are not included. If you'd like to see it, I could show you on Saturday morning. Shall we say eleven o'clock?

qs.q: How much is the rent?
When can the caller see the flat?

items.title: Exam instructions
items.say: Right, here's what you need to do before the exam. First, bring your passport or ID card; without it they won't let you in. Arrive at least thirty minutes early, because the doors close at nine fifteen. You can't take your phone into the room, so leave it in your bag. The writing part lasts ninety minutes, and then there's a short break before the speaking test.

qs.q: When do the doors close?
How long does the writing part last?

sets.name: Real-life listening
sets.about: Natural, faster speech with changes of plan and distracting numbers.

items.title: A message from a colleague
items.say: Hi, it's Dan from the language centre. Listen, I've just heard that Mr Clarke's workshop has been moved. It was supposed to be on the twelfth, but it's now on the twenty-first, which, to be honest, suits me better. It'll still be in room three-oh-four, though, so no change there. Could you let your students know? And if you wouldn't mind, bring about thirty copies of the handout. Cheers.

qs.q: When is the workshop now?
How many handouts should the listener bring?

items.title: A train cancellation
items.say: Ladies and gentlemen, this is an update for passengers on the seven forty service to Bristol. Due to a signal failure near Reading, this train has been cancelled. The next train will depart from platform six at eight twenty-five, and your tickets will be valid on that service. If you're connecting to Cardiff, please speak to a member of staff, as you may miss your connection. We apologise for any inconvenience.

qs.q: Why has the train been cancelled?
When will the next train depart?

items.title: A hectic week
items.say: It's been a hectic week, to be honest. On Monday my laptop crashed in the middle of a lesson, so I had to carry on with a book. Then on Wednesday, I'd arranged to meet Helen for lunch, but she cancelled at the last minute. I ended up going to the cinema on my own, which was actually quite nice. Anyway, I'm hoping things calm down by the weekend, because we're driving up to my parents' on Saturday.

qs.q: What happened on Monday?
What did she do on Wednesday?
o: She went to the cinema alone

items.title: A hotel booking call
items.say: Right, so, I've spoken to the hotel and they can offer us a room for the nineteenth to the twenty-second, but only if we confirm by Friday. It's a hundred and ninety pounds a night, including breakfast. Mind you, that's about twenty pounds more than last year. The conference centre is a fifteen-minute walk away, so we won't need a taxi. Could you let me know by noon tomorrow?

qs.q: How much is the room per night?
By when must they confirm the booking?
